group.passage:
Look at most keyboards, and you will see the same six letters across the top row: Q, W, E, R, T, Y. This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance. It dates back to the typewriters of the 1870s, whose metal arms could crash into each other and get stuck when a typist worked too quickly. Exactly how the letters were arranged is still debated, but a popular explanation is that letters often typed together were placed far apart. [[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.
In the 1930s, an American professor named August Dvorak designed a new layout that put the most common letters on the middle row, right under the fingers. Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed. Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.
Today's phones have no metal arms that could ever get stuck, yet their screens still show the old pattern. QWERTY's success has little to do with being the best design; it won simply because it came [[5]].

tags.key_phrase: Whatever the reason (was)（不管原因是什麼）
never replaced …, and neither did …（代動詞 did）
come first（最先出現、搶先一步）

1.explanation_zh: come about 是「（事情）發生、形成」。這種奇怪的字母順序並不是偶然形成的，下一句就交代它源自 1870 年代的打字機，字母是刻意安排的。
evidence: This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance.
It dates back to the typewriters of the 1870s

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・CN】come across 常和 by chance 一起出現（come across something by chance＝偶然碰到某物），但那要由人當主詞、後面接受詞；這裡的主詞是 order（順序），後面也沒有受詞，說不通。
option_notes_zh.B: bring about 是「造成、引起」，是及物的動詞片語，後面必須接受詞；而且主詞 order 不是去造成某件事的一方。
option_notes_zh.D: go off 是「（警報）響起、（炸彈）爆炸」，與字母順序如何形成無關。

1.strategy_zh: 主詞是 This strange order（這種順序），空格後接 by chance，沒有受詞：要選表示「（某事）發生、形成」的不及物片語。下一句交代它的來源，可以確認。線索在本句與下一句。
hints: 主詞是「這種字母順序」，空格後面沒有受詞。
下一句說這種順序是從哪裡來的？
要選表示「發生、形成」的 come 片語。

2.explanation_zh: Whatever the original reason 是 Whatever the original reason was 的省略，意思是「不管最初的原因是什麼」。前一句說字母當初怎麼排列至今仍有爭議，所以接著說：無論原因為何，打字學校教了這種排法、辦公室買了這種打字機，久而久之數百萬人都把它背得滾瓜爛熟。
evidence: Exactly how the letters were arranged is still debated
[[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.

option_notes_zh.B: 【強誘答・GN】However 常放在句首當轉折副詞，學生容易直覺選它；但 however 後面要接逗號和完整的句子，或接形容詞、副詞（however hard），不能直接接名詞片語 the original reason。
option_notes_zh.C: Whenever（每當……的時候）講的是時間，後面也要接子句，不能只接名詞片語，「每當最初的原因」不通。
option_notes_zh.D: Wherever（無論在哪裡）講的是地點，同樣要接子句，也與「原因」無關。

2.strategy_zh: 空格後只有名詞片語 the original reason，再接逗號和主要子句：這是「Whatever＋名詞（＋be）」的讓步結構，等於 No matter what the original reason was。前一句說原因有爭議，正好用「不管原因為何」帶過。線索在前一句與本句。
hints: 空格後面是名詞片語 the original reason，不是完整的子句。
前一句說字母的排列方式怎麼了？
要選可以直接接名詞、表示「不管是什麼」的字。

3.explanation_zh: neither＋助動詞＋主詞 表示「……也不」，助動詞要承接前面否定的動詞。前面是過去式 never replaced QWERTY，所以用代動詞 did：neither did any of the other designs (replace QWERTY)，也就是後來的其他設計也都沒有取代 QWERTY。
evidence: Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed.

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・GN】were 是 be 動詞，主詞 designs 又是複數，看起來很合；但 neither 承接的是一般動詞 never replaced，不是 be 動詞，要用 did 代替。
option_notes_zh.B: had 用來承接完成式（had replaced），前面是簡單過去式 never replaced，沒有完成式可以承接。
option_notes_zh.C: are 是現在式 be 動詞，時態和動詞種類都與前面的 never replaced 不符。

3.strategy_zh: 找出 neither 前面那個否定的動詞：never replaced（過去式的一般動詞）→ 代動詞用 did。不要被較前面的 it was faster 帶走，neither 承接的是否定句。線索在本句。
hints: neither 承接的是前面哪一個否定的動作？
never replaced 是什麼時態、什麼種類的動詞？
過去式的一般動詞要用哪個助動詞來代替？

4.explanation_zh: grow used to 是「逐漸習慣」。一旦整個社會都習慣了某一套系統，改用新的就代價太高，因為（since 子句）每位打字員都得從頭學起；這也呼應第一段「數百萬人都把 QWERTY 背得滾瓜爛熟」。
evidence: Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.
in time millions of people knew it by heart

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・LR】grown tired of（厭倦了）看似可以說明為什麼要換系統，但厭倦只會讓人更想換；本句說的是「換系統代價太高」，原因是大家都已經學會、用慣了，因果方向相反。
option_notes_zh.C: grown out of 是「長大後不再適合、擺脫了」，如果社會已經擺脫了這套系統，就談不上換系統代價太高。
option_notes_zh.D: made fun of 是「取笑」，取笑一套系統不會讓改用新系統變得昂貴，也和 since 子句的理由無關。

4.strategy_zh: since 子句交代了「代價太高」的原因：每位打字員都得重學。要「重學」，表示大家原本已經學會、用慣了這套系統。線索在本句的 since 子句與第一段的 knew it by heart。
hints: 為什麼換系統的代價會太高？看 since 後面。
要「重新學」，表示大家原本和這套系統是什麼關係？
要選表示「逐漸習慣」的片語。

5.explanation_zh: come first 是「最先出現、搶先一步」。QWERTY 在 1870 年代就隨打字機普及，比 1930 年代的 Dvorak 等設計早了幾十年；一旦大家都用慣了，就很難再換。所以文章說它的勝利和是不是最好的設計關係不大，只是因為它「先來」。
evidence: It dates back to the typewriters of the 1870s
In the 1930s, an American professor named August Dvorak designed a new layout
QWERTY's success has little to do with being the best design; it won simply because it came [[5]].

option_notes_zh.A: 【強誘答・CN】came close 是慣用語「差一點就成功」，但本句說 QWERTY 已經 won（贏了），「因為差一點成功所以贏了」自相矛盾。
option_notes_zh.B: came true 是「（願望、預言）實現」，主詞是鍵盤排法，不是願望，語意不通。
option_notes_zh.C: came alive 是「變得生動、活躍起來」，無法說明 QWERTY 為什麼能勝出。

5.strategy_zh: 這格要整合全文的時間線：1870 年代的打字機 → 數百萬人背熟 → 1930 年代才出現新設計 → 大家用慣了就換不掉。分號前已經排除「設計最好」這個原因，剩下的就是「出現得早」。線索在第一、二段（距離超過兩句）。
hints: QWERTY 出現在哪個年代？Dvorak 的設計又是哪個年代？
第二段說，大家習慣一套系統之後，要換新的會怎樣？
分號前說不是因為設計最好，那是因為它「最……」？

translation_zh.text:
看看大多數的鍵盤，你會在最上排看到同樣六個字母：Q、W、E、R、T、Y。這種奇怪的順序被稱為 QWERTY，它並不是偶然形成的。它可以追溯到 1870 年代的打字機：打字員打得太快時，打字機的金屬臂會互相撞在一起而卡住。這些字母究竟是怎麼排列的，至今仍有爭議，但一個流行的說法是，經常一起打出的字母被刻意分開擺放。不管最初的原因是什麼，打字學校教這種排法，辦公室買用這種排法的機器，久而久之，數百萬人都把它背得滾瓜爛熟。
1930 年代，一位名叫德沃夏克（August Dvorak）的美國教授設計了一種新的排法，把最常用的字母放在中間那一排，就在手指正下方。支持者聲稱它打起來更快、更不累，但它從來沒有取代 QWERTY，後來的其他設計也都沒有。一旦整個社會都習慣了某一套系統，改用別的系統代價就太高了，因為每一位打字員都得從頭學起。
今天的手機沒有任何會卡住的金屬臂，螢幕上卻仍然顯示這種老排法。QWERTY 的成功和它是不是最好的設計關係不大；它之所以勝出，只是因為它出現得最早。

evidence: This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance.
1.explanation_zh: 空格需要不及物動詞片語，主詞是 this strange order，意為「這個順序不是偶然『產生』的」，come about（發生、產生）正確；bring about 是及物（導致某事），come across 偶遇，go off 爆炸／響起，皆不合。

evidence: Exactly how the letters were arranged is still debated, but a popular explanation is that letters often typed together were placed far apart.
[[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.
2.explanation_zh: 前文說原因仍有爭議，接著說「不論最初原因為何」，大家都學了這種排列；Whatever the original reason (was) 是常見省略句型；However 後需接形容詞或副詞，Whenever、Wherever 與 reason 不搭配。

evidence: Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed.
3.explanation_zh: neither + 助動詞 + 主詞 的倒裝，承接前句的一般動詞過去式 replaced，助動詞用 did（= none of the other designs replaced it either）；were、had、are 時態或助動詞種類不合。

evidence: Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.
4.explanation_zh: 一旦整個社會「習慣了」某一套系統，換掉就代價太高，因為每個人都要重學，故選 grown used to；grown tired of 厭倦了應該會想換，與 switching becomes too costly 的邏輯不符；grown out of 長大不再適用、made fun of 嘲笑，皆不合。

evidence: QWERTY's success has little to do with being the best design; it won simply because it came [[5]].
5.explanation_zh: 全文論點是 QWERTY 不是最好的設計，而是因為最早出現、先被大家學會而勝出，came first「先出現」；came close 差一點、came true 實現、came alive 變得生動，都不合文意。

evidence: This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance.
1.explanation_zh: didn't come about by chance 表示「並非偶然發生」；bring about 是及物用法，不合；come across/go off 語意不對。

evidence: [[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.
2.explanation_zh: Whatever the original reason（不論原本的理由為何）是讓步結構，後面說學校仍然教這個排列；However/Whenever/Wherever 都接不上 the original reason。

evidence: Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed.
3.explanation_zh: neither 置於句首要倒裝，且前句動詞是過去式一般動詞 replaced，所以助動詞用 did。

evidence: Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.
4.explanation_zh: 整個社會一旦習慣（grown used to）某個系統，要改就很花成本；其他選項語意與「switching becomes too costly」不合。

evidence: QWERTY's success has little to do with being the best design; it won simply because it came [[5]].
5.explanation_zh: 前文說 QWERTY 成功與設計最佳無關，只是因為它最先出現，came first。

A.evidence: This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance.
A.explanation_zh: come across 作「偶然碰到」要人當主詞並接受詞；不及物時是「（訊息）被理解」，「這種順序不是偶然被理解的」不通，下一句交代的是它的來源。

B.evidence: This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance.
B.explanation_zh: bring about（造成）是及物片語，主動語態後面必須接受詞；本句 didn't ___ by chance 後沒有受詞。

D.evidence: This strange order, known as QWERTY, didn't [[1]] by chance.
D.explanation_zh: go off 是「爆炸、（警報）響起」，與字母順序如何形成無關。

B.evidence: [[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.
B.explanation_zh: however 作讓步時要接形容詞或副詞再接子句（however hard …），不能直接接名詞片語 the original reason。

C.evidence: [[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.
C.explanation_zh: whenever 是連接詞，後面要接子句；而且講時間，「每當最初的原因」不通。

D.evidence: [[2]] the original reason, typing schools taught the layout, offices bought machines that used it, and in time millions of people knew it by heart.
D.explanation_zh: wherever 是連接詞，後面要接子句；講地點，也與 reason 不搭。

A.evidence: Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed.
A.explanation_zh: neither 承接的是前面一般動詞過去式 never replaced，倒裝的助動詞要用代動詞 did，不能用 be 動詞 were。

B.evidence: Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed.
B.explanation_zh: 前面是簡單過去式 never replaced，沒有完成式可承接；而且 the other designs that followed 在 Dvorak 之後，用過去完成式時序也錯。

C.evidence: Its supporters claimed it was faster and less tiring, but it never replaced QWERTY, and neither [[3]] any of the other designs that followed.
C.explanation_zh: are 是現在式 be 動詞，動詞種類與時態都和 never replaced 不符。

A.evidence: Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.

C.evidence: Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.
C.explanation_zh: grow out of 是「長大後不再適合、擺脫」；已經擺脫的系統就談不上「改用別的代價太高」。

D.evidence: Once a whole society has [[4]] one system, switching becomes too costly, since every typist would have to learn again from the beginning.
D.explanation_zh: 取笑一套系統和「每位打字員都得從頭學」這個換系統的代價無關。

A.evidence: QWERTY's success has little to do with being the best design; it won simply because it came [[5]].
A.explanation_zh: came close 是「差一點就成功」，但本句說 it won（贏了），「因為差一點成功所以贏了」自相矛盾。

B.evidence: QWERTY's success has little to do with being the best design; it won simply because it came [[5]].
B.explanation_zh: come true 的主詞是願望、預言，鍵盤排法不會「實現」，也無法說明勝出的原因。

C.explanation_zh: came alive（變得生動）無法說明勝出原因；文中交代 QWERTY 在 1870 年代就有、Dvorak 的設計到 1930 年代才出現，勝出的理由是出現得早。
